item.title: Iran War Live Updates: Oil and Gas Prices Soar After New Attacks on Gulf Energy Sites
item.summary: Refineries and gas facilities in Kuwait, Qatar and Saudi Arabia were struck, a day after Iran’s vast South Pars gas field was hit. The sustained attacks heightened fears over the war’s damage to the global economy.

item.title: The Iran War’s Economic Threat to Europe and Asia
item.summary: Inflation and its consequences for growth are a growing concern for countries where memories of the 2022 energy crisis are fresh.

item.title: A Lebanese Cafe on the Edge of Destruction
item.summary: Near the center of Beirut, one image captures the aftermath of an Israeli strike.

item.title: For U.S., Unmet Expectations in Iran Fit a Familiar Pattern in the Region
item.summary: Iran’s military retaliation, along with the political defiance of its new leaders, evokes a decades-old pattern of unrealized goals for American interventions in the region.

item.title: Netanyahu Hopes Strikes on Iran Will Lead to Uprising and Regime Change
item.summary: Israeli attacks have targeted the command centers of Iran’s repressive, internal security forces in hopes that Iranians will overthrow their rulers. Some see that as wishful thinking.

item.title: Trump Says U.S. and Qatar Not Involved in Strike on Iran’s South Pars Gas Field
item.summary: President Trump said Israel was responsible for the attack, but vowed to “massively” destroy the gas field if Tehran hit Qatar’s energy facilities in retaliation.

item.title: Pakistan Pauses Afghanistan Airstrikes for Eid
item.summary: At least 143 people were killed in a Pakistani airstrike that hit a drug rehabilitation facility in Kabul on Monday, according to a top U.N. official.

item.title: The Soldier Who Came Back From the Dead
item.summary: Told that Nazar Daletskyi had died, his Ukrainian family buried what they thought were his remains. He turned up three years later in a prisoner-of-war exchange.

item.title: E.U. Loan for Ukraine Becomes Election Leverage for Orban
item.summary: European leaders are pushing Prime Minister Viktor Orban to stop blocking a €90 billion loan to Ukraine. But the issue is a rallying cry in remarkably close elections in Hungary set for April 12.

item.title: In Swaths of Germany, the Far-Right AfD Is Part of the Fabric
item.summary: The Alternative for Germany party, or AfD, is shunned in federal politics but is a regional force. This fall, it could win broader power for the first time.
